selection_reasons.method: Use the B3LYP hybrid functional (20% HF exchange) for this closed-shell organic conformational scan; the ORCA manual entry documents B3LYP as a popular hybrid functional. No dispersion correction is claimed because the retrieved official excerpt does not document one.
selection_reasons.basis: Use the Karlsruhe def2-TZVP polarized valence triple-zeta orbital basis, available for H–Rn, as a balanced basis for carbon/hydrogen conformational energies.

normalization.cost_reasoning: Method/basis rationale has no runtime estimate or seven-point/1200 s feasibility accounting.

criterion.verbatim: Criterion stated before scanning: use the 60-degree grid; if the lowest-energy converged grid point has at least one neighboring interval with |DeltaE| > 5 kJ/mol, or any adjacent converged pair differs by > 10 kJ/mol, propose at most two additional constrained optimizations at midpoint angles adjacent to the minimum or steepest interval. If the minimum is bracketed by neighbor differences <= 5 kJ/mol on both sides, or no converged points exist, stop without extra angles.
static_limitations: Literal refinement trigger (any adjacent change >10) can coincide with literal stop condition (minimum bracketed by <=5 on both sides); no precedence is declared.
Generated recommendation checks only max_adj_delta >10 and otherwise states no >5 minimum-neighbor trigger, without computing the 5 kJ/mol branch.
This is pre-execution static review of the approved code, not scientific correctness or successful output validation.
